Second-line agents: rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 doses, or cyclophosphamide

Cetirizine + lorazepam: additive sedation; usually minor.
Levetiracetam: no clinically significant interaction with the oral contraceptive, acyclovir, methylprednisolone or IVIG.

output.query: anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosis treatment ovarian teratoma

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titers related more closely to outcome than serum titers.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumor, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumor removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: About 70% of patients have prodromal headache, fever or a viral-like illness before psychiatric symptoms, seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability and hypoventilation develop.
results.source: Dalmau J et al. Lancet Neurol 2011;10:63-74

output.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumor removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 positive (1:160); sodium 133 mEq/L; thyroid function, thyroid antibodies, other neuronal and onconeural antibodies negative; beta-hCG negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain the reviewed serum work-up, including a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay that must be interpreted with CSF rather than alone
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes metabolic, thyroid, toxic and infective mimics, checks pregnancy before treatment and gives the serum anti-GluN1 result, which is read with the CSF assay.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Bilateral medial temporal FLAIR hyperintensity, left greater than right, and subtle insular signal, without restricted diffusion, hemorrhage or enhancement
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination before LP in a febrile patient with seizures and fluctuating consciousness; it does not confirm the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: 59 lymphocytic cells/uL, protein 78.3 mg/dL, 6 CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands; HSV-1/2 PCR negative; CSF anti-GluN1 IgG positive 1:320
action_criteria.label: Analyze CSF for cells, protein and glucose, OCB or IgG index, HSV PCR and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay interpreted in parallel with serum
action_criteria.rationale: The CSF cell-based anti-GluN1 assay is the decisive test, and the HSV PCR excludes the infectious mimic suggested by the fever and medial temporal signal.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Extreme delta brush, generalized rhythmic delta activity and two left temporal electrographic seizures with behavioral arrest
action_criteria.label: Obtain EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, explicitly assessing for extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: Two generalized seizures and staring episodes with behavioral arrest need an EEG for seizures, encephalopathy and extreme delta brush.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right ovarian 1.8 cm mature cystic teratoma
action_criteria.label: Screen for an ovarian teratoma with pelvic and abdominal ultrasound
action_criteria.rationale: Young women carry the highest teratoma risk; tumor removal is part of first-line treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Seizure burden and evolution of the background over 24 hours or more
action_criteria.label: Escalate to continuous EEG monitoring for seizure burden and non-convulsive seizures
action_criteria.rationale: Two seizures in a 30-minute routine EEG and repeated staring episodes with behavioral arrest call for continuous monitoring of the seizure burden.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Contraceptive thrombotic caution; no prohibitive interaction
action_criteria.label: Check interactions between the planned treatment and her combined oral contraceptive
action_criteria.rationale: Estrogen adds to the thrombotic risk of IVIG and immobility; it does not change the choice of immunotherapy.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.label: Optionally consult the published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; no clinical decision in this case depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1 to 2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, given the fever and medial temporal signal, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges).
Arrange prompt surgical removal of the right ovarian teratoma (laparoscopic, ovary-sparing where feasible) as part of first-line treatment, with gynecology.

Start an antiseizure medication such as levetiracetam or lacosamide, with a benzodiazepine for seizures lasting more than 5 minutes; avoid valproate in a woman able to become pregnant; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.
Admit to a neurology ward with seizure precautions and continuous cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide; discuss fertility preservation before cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation and insomnia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first.
Stop the combined oral contraceptive while she is bed-bound and receiving IVIG (venous thromboembolism risk) and give VTE prophylaxis.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioral management; gynecology for the teratoma.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

differential.diagnosis: Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1) or other viral encephalitis
differential.key_features: Fever 38.4 and medial temporal signal, but CSF HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV and enterovirus PCR negative; no hemorrhage or restricted diffusion on MRI; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.
Fever and mild leukocytosis, but a lymphocytic CSF with normal glucose ratio, negative Gram stain and culture, and a two-week course.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B or AMPA receptor)
differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel negative (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA, DPPX) and onconeural antibodies negative; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.
Generalized seizures, orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic instability, extreme delta brush and CSF pleocytosis with oligoclonal bands are not explained by a psychiatric disorder.

differential.diagnosis: Drug-induced psychosis or neuroleptic malignant syndrome
differential.key_features: No antipsychotic or new drug (one dose of lorazepam only); urine drug screen and alcohol negative; CK only 179 U/L.

key_clinical_evidence: Subacute onset over 2 weeks, after a febrile viral-like prodrome, of paranoia and behavioral change, paraphasic speech with echolalia, generalized seizures, orofacial dyskinesias and choreoathetosis, fluctuating consciousness and autonomic instability: all six Graus 2016 groups.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:320) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016); serum positive 1:160 is read with the CSF.

MRI shows bilateral medial temporal (left greater than right) and insular FLAIR signal without restricted diffusion, hemorrhage or enhancement; the negative CSF HSV PCR excludes HSV encephalitis despite the fever.
EEG shows extreme delta brush, generalized rhythmic delta and two left temporal seizures with behavioral arrest; extreme delta brush, when present, supports but does not establish the diagnosis.
Pelvic ultrasound shows a 1.8 cm right ovarian mature cystic teratoma: its removal is part of first-line treatment.
Earlier immunotherapy and tumor removal are associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A viral-like prodrome precedes about 70% of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it does not establish viral encephalitis, which CSF PCR addresses.
red_herrings.data_point: Upper respiratory illness with low-grade fevers three weeks before the neuropsychiatric syndrome.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a primary viral encephalitis (HSV) or post-viral psychosis; tempts the agent to commit to empiric antiviral therapy without pursuing autoimmune workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Seizures, orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG and CSF inflammation accompany the behavioral change and must be explained before a psychiatric diagnosis is accepted.
red_herrings.data_point: Acute psychiatric presentation (irritability, anxiety, paranoid beliefs, withdrawal) in a previously well 24-year-old with no psychiatric history.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a primary psychiatric diagnosis (first-episode psychosis, brief psychotic disorder) and delays neurologic workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatremia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing instead of the neurological work-up.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome needs antipsychotic exposure and a markedly raised CK; this mild rise reflects seizures and dyskinesias and does not change management.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Raises concern for neuroleptic malignant syndrome or rhabdomyolysis when combined with dyskinesias and hyperthermia.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive confusion, seizures, and abnormal movements over two weeks

patient.history_present_illness: This 24-year-old right-handed woman was brought to the emergency department by her partner and mother after two weeks of progressively worsening behavioral changes, confusion, and new-onset seizures. Approximately three weeks ago, the patient developed a mild upper respiratory illness with low-grade fevers, sore throat, malaise, and rhinorrhea lasting 4-5 days, for which she did not seek medical attention. She appeared to recover, but approximately one week later her partner noticed personality changes: she became increasingly irritable, anxious, and paranoid, expressing unfounded beliefs that her classmates were plotting against her. She stopped attending her graduate classes and became withdrawn. Over the following days, she developed progressive confusion, insomnia, and difficulty finding words. Five days prior to presentation, she had her first witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting approximately 90 seconds with post-ictal confusion lasting 30 minutes. She was taken to an outside emergency department where she was given lorazepam 2 mg IV and discharged with a referral to neurology. Over the subsequent days, her condition deteriorated rapidly. She developed repetitive lip-smacking and jaw movements that her family initially mistook for a medication side effect. She became increasingly agitated with periods of unresponsiveness alternating with combative episodes. On the day of presentation, her partner witnessed a second generalized seizure and called emergency services. In the emergency department, the patient was noted to have fluctuating levels of consciousness, prominent orofacial dyskinesias, intermittent tachycardia, and blood pressure lability. She was unable to provide a coherent history. Her partner reports no prior psychiatric history, no recent travel, no tick bites, no new medications, and no illicit drug use.

neurological_exam.additional: Prominent orofacial dyskinesias with stereotyped lip-smacking, tongue protrusion, and jaw movements. Intermittent choreoathetoid movements of the upper extremities bilaterally. Episodes of autonomic instability observed during examination including transient tachycardia to 130 bpm and blood pressure fluctuations. Two brief episodes of staring with behavioral arrest lasting approximately 15 seconds each observed during the encounter, concerning for subclinical seizures.
neurological_exam.coordination: Unable to perform finger-to-nose or heel-to-shin testing reliably due to encephalopathy and involuntary movements.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive, 3 mm bilaterally. Extraocular movements intact without nystagmus. Facial sensation intact to light touch. Mild bilateral facial weakness noted with decreased nasolabial fold depth. Hearing grossly intact. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue midline. Prominent orofacial dyskinesias with repetitive lip-smacking and jaw movements observed throughout the examination.
neurological_exam.gait: Unable to assess; patient is bed-bound due to altered mental status and agitation.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but disoriented to date and place. Intermittently agitated, with periods of unresponsiveness lasting 20-30 seconds. Speech is disorganized with paraphasic errors and echolalia. Unable to follow multi-step commands. Montreal Cognitive Assessment attempted but patient unable to cooperate. Short-term memory severely impaired; unable to recall any of 3 objects at 5 minutes.
neurological_exam.motor: Tone increased in bilateral upper extremities with intermittent rigidity. Strength 4/5 throughout when patient cooperates, though limited by inconsistent effort due to encephalopathy. No frank hemiparesis. Intermittent dystonic posturing of the left hand observed.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally, brachioradialis 2+ bilaterally, patellar 3+ bilaterally, Achilles 2+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Withdraws symmetrically to pain in all four extremities. Detailed sensory examination limited by encephalopathy.
